newsitem.title: USA: N.J. picks two bond counsel firms on $3.4 bln deal.
newsitem.headline: N.J. picks two bond counsel firms on $3.4 bln deal.

text.p: New Jersey officials said Wednesday they selected Blank Rome Comisky & McCauley, of Cherry Hill, and Riker Danzig Scherer Hyland & Perretti, of Morristown, to act as bond counsel on the state's proposed $3.4 billion pension obligation bond deal.

"These law firms have combined experience with prior state bond issues and complex financings that will be invaluable to the development of the proposed pension bond issue," state Attorney General Peter Verniero said in a statement.

Verniero said total hourly billings for Blank Rome will be capped at $175,000, unless bonds are offered in more than one sale as some advisers have suggested. In that case, fees will for the additional bonds will be capped at $40,000.
Riker Danzig's fees will be capped at $85,000 for one issue and $20,000 for any additional deal.
The state has already selected Merrill Lynch & Co to act as senior manager on the deal, and Public Resources Advisory Group is the financial adviser.
The proposed bond deal, which still requires legislative approval, has sparked controversy in the state over whether the sale would be fiscally prudent.
Opponents charge that the bonds, which will be used to eliminate the pension system's $4 billion unfunded liability, are a gimmick to generate short-term budget savings for Gov Christine Whitman.
Whitman said a bond deal is a cheaper method of paying off the liability than other alternatives.
Merrill has said that an April 1 sale date for the bonds would help New Jersey capitalize on current low rates, but lawmakers have said that date is unrealistic.
